# Chapter Fourteen (dirty)

I poured tea for Adrian Voss, who preferred tea to coffee these days and never
touched the black stuff. Helen Carr, the solicitor who shares his cases, took
notes in her notebook.

Mrs. Bramley, still only thirty and newly widowed, brought up the tray. Voss
had moved his rooms to Harbour Street above the bookshop — Number Seven on Grey
Lane was long abandoned.

The Amber Circle, we learned, meets in Baker Street now, not Harbour Street.
Carr recorded the change before the constable arrived.
